lines.text: Today you will store many things in one variable and use it to build Rock, Paper, Scissors.
A list keeps many values in order inside square brackets, like team = ["Aarav", "Meera", "Kabir"].
Each item has a position called its index.
The first item is team[0], the second is team[1]. team[-1] gives the last item.
team.append("Zoya") adds Zoya to the end of the list. len(team) tells you how many items it has now.
for player in team: visits every item, one at a time.
"Zoya" in team gives True or False, so you can check if something is in the list.
Square brackets make a list, and commas separate the items.
Index zero is the first player, Aarav, and index two is the third player, Kabir.
Append adds Zoya to the end of the list.
Then len counts the items, so now the team has four players.
The for loop visits each snack in the list, one after another.
We never need to know the index numbers. Python handles them for us.
The word in checks whether banana is one of the moves.
It is not, so the program politely says it is not a move.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
